observations.location: release/public-alpha/assets/site.css (shared `table { display: block; overflow-x: auto }` at the 760px query), as it renders the opening element map under sec:opening and the comparison table under sec:comparison
observations.note: At 390 px the three-column map is 425 px wide in a 342 px measure, so its 'What it says' column (131 px, two or three words a line) is partly behind a horizontal scroll. The four-column comparison is 498 px wide, so the third reading's column is off-screen until scrolled. The published Claude Twenty-first Sunday edition measures the same, so this is shared site styling and not this conversion. The no-clip treatment decided for the dossier on 2026-09-23 does not reach the proper-study map or comparison tables, which may be a missing criterion for those tables.

observations.note: The generated Passage labels mix 'Ps 71:1' with 'Psalms 71:8,11', 'Psalms 2:8' and 'Psalms 28:10–11', and set verse lists without a space after the comma. The study prose writes 'Ps 71:8, 11'. The same mix appears in the published Claude Twenty-first Sunday edition, so this is a cosmetic matter of the shared generator, not of this leaf.

summary: Reviewed the canonical web edition build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/f01-christ-the-king.md, conversion hash e7bc1c594ffc3f63b40493237770ab232ad338a46ef6c9a3000abefe4041af22 as research/web-artifact.json records it and as the file's bytes give. I compared it with the reviewed research PDF (build/claude/.../f01-christ-the-king.pdf, sha256 444c7e0c…, matching research/artifacts.json, as do all 27 sealed render inputs) and with the canonical sources. Checks: (1) The full word streams of PDF and Markdown, normalized and compared, differ only by layout: running heads, page numbers, the printed Contents, bullets, the order of table cells in the extracted text, and the verse-sign glyph. There is no omission or addition apart from the converter's usual title and description lines. (2) All 54 source headings keep their levels: sections and the three properlane readings are h2, subsections h3. The 10 TOC links match the PDF Contents and resolve. The 11 proper-<key> anchors and every id are unique. (3) Every \latin/\work/\emph/\textit argument (317) stands in italics, and the bold element names and scope leads match \textbf. (4) Each reading closes with its own four-sense definition list (12 dt/dd), as in the PDF. (5) The map, comparison and nine-row orientation-v2 tables match the PDF row for row. The 26 quotations render as 26 separate blockquotes, ℣ and the accented Latin are readable, and .nodecor and smallcaps cues hold. (6) There is no TeX debris, no trailing whitespace and no production metadata. The Last-revised timestamp and the rights colophon are present. (7) A fresh tools/tpt web-edition conversion into my scratch directory is byte-identical, and check-web-edition validates the declaration. (8) For the browser review, I rendered the page through the site's own render_page (preview mode, pinned Markdown 3.10.3) with assets/site.css. I captured full-page headless-Chromium screenshots at 1280 px and 390 px. There is no page-level horizontal overflow at either width. At 390 px I did the passage-to-occurrence/place/date lookup on the orientation table, Colossians 1:12–20 → Paul writes in bonds to Colossa, captivity letters placed at Rome → Disputed: A.D. 61; A.D. 61–63, and it pairs correctly under the three-column dossier rule. Limits: I made no full site build and checked no catalog or navigation. I used only one browser engine. The PDF comparison rests on extracted text, with formatting checked separately against the source. I did not re-collate the Latin or English against their witnesses; earlier reviews own that. Verdict: PASS. These exact bytes may go to installation.
